biography: Max "Havoc" Gordon didn't grow up on a racetrack; he was forged in the Mojave Desert. His father, a former miner, taught him to drive a beat-up pickup truck before he could ride a bike. Early mornings were spent navigating treacherous desert trails, learning to read the terrain and push machines to their absolute limit. This raw, instinctive understanding of vehicle dynamics translated seamlessly when, at 16, he entered his first amateur off-road race with a borrowed truck and a whole lot of audacity. He rolled the truck twice but still managed to finish third, covered in dust and grinning like a maniac. That day, the desert lost a potential geologist and racing gained a wild card. Now, at 21, Max is tearing up the Super Trophy Trucks circuit, a rising star known for his fearless driving and disregard for mechanical sympathy. He's proving that talent forged in the desert can conquer any track.
drivingStyle: Max's driving style can be best described as controlled chaos. He attacks corners with reckless abandon, trusting his instincts and vehicle control over calculated strategy. He rarely brakes, preferring to use the throttle to steer and power-slide through turns. Tire management is not his forte; he prioritizes raw speed and aggressive maneuvers, often pushing his tires to their limit in the early stages of a race. Under pressure, he becomes even more aggressive, thriving in chaotic situations and relishing the opportunity to make daring overtakes. He is a high-risk, high-reward driver, thrilling to watch but prone to spectacular crashes.

rivalries.reason: Alvarez represents the opposite of Max: calculated, precise, and methodical. Their contrasting styles often lead to tense on-track battles and clashes of personality off the track.
A fierce competitor, Ava and Max have a history of trading paint and aggressive maneuvers. Their rivalry is fueled by mutual respect and a desire to prove who is the faster driver.
Williams, a veteran of the sport, sees Max as an upstart who lacks respect for the traditions of racing. Max, in turn, views Williams as old-fashioned and too cautious.

quirks: Always wears a lucky bandana given to him by his father before every race.
Listens to heavy metal at ear-splitting volume right before the start to get pumped up.
Refuses to wash his racing suit during a race weekend, believing it holds the dust of past victories.
famousQuote: "You gotta drive like you stole it, and remember, second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Silver State 300 off-road race in his rookie year, beating several established veterans in a borrowed truck.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Super Trophy Trucks championship race due to an overly aggressive maneuver, costing him the title.
